summary.short: Federal statute (Pub. L. 119-21) whose AI-relevant provisions appropriate funds for federal AI and automation uses, direct the Secretary to implement AI tools against Medicare improper payments by 2027, and bar states and political subdivisions from enforcing AI-regulating laws for ten years after enactment.
summary.long: The excerpted AI-relevant sections of Pub. L. 119-21 are mainly appropriations and public-sector duties. Sec. 43201 appropriates $500,000,000 to the Department of Commerce for FY2025, available until September 30, 2034, to modernize federal IT with commercial AI and automated decision systems. Subsection (c) bars states and political subdivisions, for 10 years from enactment, from enforcing laws that regulate AI models, AI systems or automated decision systems entered into interstate commerce, with exceptions for laws that facilitate deployment without substantive requirements, cost-based fees, and provisions carrying criminal penalties. Subsection (d) defines these terms. Sec. 112204 adds Social Security Act Sec. 1899D, requiring the Secretary to implement AI tools to reduce and recoup Medicare Parts A and B improper payments by January 1, 2027, with annual reports from 2029. Sec. 50404 directs the Secretary of Energy to curate Department of Energy scientific data for AI and develop AI models, with $150,000,000 available through September 30, 2026. Sec. 60003(b) bars use of certain CBP funds for surveillance towers not tested and accepted to deliver autonomous capabilities. Defense, CBP, nuclear and rural health sections appropriate funds for AI-related uses, and Sec. 71401 lists artificial intelligence among permitted rural health program uses.

notes: Excerpt of several sections of the act; the registry's Pub. L. 119-21 and H. Con. Res. 14 references do not appear in the excerpted text, so no enacted_by_bill relation is recorded. Bracketed AGORA headers and section titles are compilation labels, not statutory text. Several sections recur in the document with different dollar amounts (e.g., Sec. 20002, 20004, 20005, 20006 each appear twice; Sec. 20005(a)(2) is $1,100,000,000 in one version and $1,400,000,000 in the other); no amounts are coded. Sec. 43201(c) imposes a 10-year moratorium on State and local laws regulating AI models, systems and automated decision systems in interstate commerce, with exceptions in (c)(2); it is not coded in this relations/entities pass.
